mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in WORKPLACES mobility into t-0w signals fewer commuter-linked trips, and that reduction suppresses discretionary retail visits over the next four weeks. If workplace activity stays below its prior three-week average, RETAIL_REC should remain lower than in the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -35.7 at t-2w to -19.7 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC stayed near -30
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean despite WORKPLACES remaining below -20% for the next four weeks, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM above zero indicates more errand-based out-of-home activity, but when it is paired with weak retail demand the effect is substitution toward necessity trips, not shopping trips. That substitution should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above 0 after a negative week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was 3.4 at t-2w then -1.9 at t-1w and 0.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays positive and RETAIL_REC increases for two consecutive weeks, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in PARKS mobility acts as a warm-weather mobility proxy that temporarily competes with retail visits, pulling discretionary time away from shopping centers. When PARKS exceeds its recent baseline by more than 20 points, RETAIL_REC should weaken within the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 20 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from 6.7 at t-3w to 36.3 at t-2w before falling to -7.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week after a PARKS spike above +20, the seasonal displacement hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT remains deeply negative while WORKPLACES are also depressed, the commuting network is not recovering enough to feed retail trips, so retail mobility should stay below the prior month. This joint weakness should predict lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed near -34 to -30 across all four weeks
fact:WORKPLACES remained negative across all four weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -20% but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean, the commuting-suppression mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An improvement in RESIDENTIAL mobility means people are spending more time at home, which reduces spontaneous shopping and leisure outings. If residential time remains elevated, RETAIL_REC should fall relative to the previous four weeks over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 10.0, 9.9, 10.6, then 8.7 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above 8% and RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks, reject the stay-at-home displacement hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals fewer multi-stop weekday trips, which directly reduces routine retail errands. The effect should be visible within one week and persist if both series stay weak.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall versus the prior week
failure_condition: If a joint weekly drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES is followed by stable or higher RETAIL_REC, the multi-stop weekday-trip mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: If retail mobility is already weak while transit remains severely depressed, reopening of shopping activity cannot fully transmit through public transport access, so the retail series should stay below baseline for the next four weeks. This is a regime-conditional persistence effect under constrained transport access.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC stayed around -31 to -23 across the snapshot
fact:TRANSIT remained below -30 in every week shown
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises toward baseline while TRANSIT stays below -30%, the transport-access persistence hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A temporary PARKS spike followed by a drop usually signals weather-driven outdoor substitution that fades quickly and then releases demand back into retail outlets. After the spike passes, RETAIL_REC should improve over the next four weeks if parks mobility normalizes.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls back below its 2-week peak after exceeding +20
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached 36.3 at t-2w and then declined to 14.0 and -7.1
failure_condition: If PARKS normalizes downward but RETAIL_REC does not rise above its last-4-week mean within four weeks, the release-back-to-retail hypothesis fails.
